title: The Landfall of Cape Reckoning
premise: Oscar Coldharbour, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers—cheerful lenders who collect in blood—chases a monsoon along the Cape Reckoning coast and discovers a sea cave exposed by an unprecedented low tide, inside which lies the wreck of the Reckoning and proof that her missing grandfather's fortune was stolen, not lost. Trapped by the storm with a leaking boat and a taciturn salvager named Ines Marlowe, who has her own claim on the cave, Oscar must decide whether to sell the evidence to the Vanes to buy her life or expose the truth and inherit nothing but her grandfather's name. As the monsoon peaks, the Vanes arrive to collect, forcing a desperate standoff in the flooding cave. Oscar survives by sacrificing the treasure itself—sinking it beyond reach—and walks out owing nothing, carrying only the truth and an unlikely ally.
about_author: Astrid Eriksen is a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting storm-battered coastlines before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a converted fishing trawler moored somewhere off the northern capes.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She launches her storm-chasing rig ahead of a monster monsoon while dodging calls from the Vane brothers, whose cheerful threats make clear her deadline is the storm's end. Establishes her skill, her recklessness, and the noose of debt. Emotional beat: bravado stretched thin over fear.

chapters.title: Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She reaches the cape her grandfather vanished near forty years ago, chasing barometric readings that promise a once-in-a-century pressure drop. A local warns her about the tide legends; she laughs him off. Emotional beat: grief disguised as scientific curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The freak low tide strips the sea away and reveals a cave mouth beneath the cliffs. Against every instinct she anchors and goes in, finding timbers stamped with the Reckoning's name. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the water begins to return.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Salvager Ines Marlowe catches Oscar looting what Ines considers her claim, having spent years searching for the cave herself. They fight, then freeze as the tide seals the entrance behind them. Emotional beat: hostility interrupted by shared entrapment.

chapters.title: Sealed In
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Trapped as the tide rises through the cave's inner channels, they discover an air pocket and the wreck's intact hold—including a ledger in Oscar's grandfather's handwriting proving his partners stole the cargo and let him drown. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Liars
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Reading the ledger by lamplight, Oscar learns the Vanes' family were among the thieves—their fortune built on her grandfather's death. The revelation reframes her debt as inheritance of a crime. Emotional beat: rage with nowhere to put it.

chapters.title: Escape at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the next low tide they blast a temporary exit using Ines's salvage charges, barely clearing the collapse. Oscar's boat takes hull damage; Ines offers her leaking ketch as shelter from the incoming monsoon. Emotional beat: survival forging fragile trust.

chapters.title: Terms of Partnership
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Holed up in a cove, they negotiate: Ines wants the wreck's salvage rights, Oscar wants the ledger made public. Neither fully trusts the other, but both know the Vanes will come when word spreads. Emotional beat: wary bargain, first flicker of respect.

chapters.title: The Vanes Send Their Regards
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A satellite call reveals the Vanes have tracked her beacon and are sending their enforcer, Corvo, with a 'settlement offer.' Oscar realizes the storm that trapped her also hid her—until now. Emotional beat: hunted feeling closing in.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The monsoon makes landfall; they ride it out anchored in mangrove shallows, repairing the ketch and drilling holes in the hull scenario after scenario. Ines reveals her father died diving for the Reckoning. Emotional beat: two griefs recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Corvo Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corvo arrives uninvited at their anchorage, all smiles, offering to forgive the debt for the ledger alone. Oscar stalls, sensing he plans to leave no witnesses. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon, fear held behind steady eyes.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines secretly photographs the ledger, planning to sell copies to a rival salvager to fund her own claim—a betrayal of their bargain. Oscar catches her. Emotional beat: trust cracked down its middle, loyalty vs. truth made literal between them.

chapters.title: Storm Anchor
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A Category-five cell forces them to run before it, Corvo's boat shadowing them. In a hair-raising passage through reef channels, Ines's seamanship saves them both, and Oscar saves Ines overboard. Emotional beat: actions rebuilding what words broke.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Hold
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Sheltering below during the worst of it, Oscar admits she nearly took Corvo's deal; Ines admits why she needs money—to raise a memorial for the divers the Vanes' ancestors killed. Emotional beat: honesty as ballast; the alliance becomes real.

chapters.title: The Map Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Repairing storm damage, they find the grandfather's hidden chart showing a second chamber in the cave holding the actual cargo—gold and documents worth enough to erase everything. Emotional beat: hope arriving like a trap.

chapters.title: Race the Falling Barometer
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With a brief weather window before the monsoon's second landfall, they race back to Cape Reckoning, Corvo one headland behind. The chapter is pure pursuit across open water. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened into focus.

chapters.title: Into the Second Chamber
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They dive the flooded passage into the second chamber and find the cargo—and her grandfather's final messages naming every thief, including the Vanes' patriarch. Then Corvo's lights appear at the cave mouth. Emotional beat: triumph ambushed.

chapters.title: The Cave Becomes a Trap
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Corvo seals the entrance with their own anchor line and starts pumping smoke inside, demanding the ledger and the gold. Rising water, failing air, and a ticking tide clock force a plan neither woman likes. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What Survives the Flood
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Climax: they use Ines's remaining charges to flood the second chamber deliberately, sinking the gold forever and blasting free as Corvo's men are caught in the collapse. Corvo drowns reaching for the treasure he came to steal. Emotional beat: sacrifice as victory.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Wrecked ashore with nothing but the ledger's copied pages, they limp to the nearest harbor where Oscar broadcasts the grandfather's testimony to authorities and press before the Vanes can silence it. Emotional beat: truth delivered at last, at cost.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The Vanes are arrested; their empire unravels as descendants of other victims come forward. Oscar owes no one. Ines receives official recognition of her father's dive site. Emotional beat: justice as quiet aftermath, not fireworks.

chapters.title: The Next Horizon
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Weeks later, Oscar and Ines refit the ketch together—not for treasure, but to chart the coast's drowned wrecks as a public memorial. Oscar finally reads her grandfather's last letter without flinching. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility freely chosen.
